correctness.rationale: Let a_i=floor(r_i/2), T=sum a_i and o=count odd r_i. The defensive inequality on a chosen peripheral vertex is 2(k_i-1+z0)+1>=r_i. If the apex is absent, global minimality forces a single nonempty blade with k_i=a_i+1. With apex present, any blade with k_i>a_i contains its own defensive suballiance, while the center requires sum k_i>=T+floor(o/2), giving k_i=a_i for all blades and o<=1. Conversely every nonempty proper subset of either proposed type fails a peripheral or apex inequality. New independent exhaustive all-subset tests exactly matched all families for seven heterogeneous bouquets; B(2,4,4) has 81 minimal sets.
residual_risks: Checks are bounded; infinite claims rest on reconstructed proof.
